projects.title: Phishing feature robustness
projects.description: How well does a phishing detector work when some of the information it relies on is missing? I compare models and study the errors caused by losing website or URL features.
projects.detail: Grouped historical-data tests and a paired screenshot/URL study examine feature reliability. In the paired study, URL ranking exceeded compact image and equal-fusion baselines. Dataset and collection limits remain; this does not establish performance on current attacks.

projects.title: Citation-support checkpoints
projects.description: When an AI answer includes citations, do those sources actually support it? I compare ways of flagging answers for review and examine simple factors, such as answer length, that can affect the results.
projects.detail: Uses ALCE sentence labels and 900 RAGTruth answers from 150 question groups. Length and generator controls complicate claims about the tested evidence-reading scores. The manuscript is a working draft, not peer reviewed.

projects.title: Early transient prioritisation
projects.description: Can the first few observations help identify which astronomical events deserve closer attention? I compare models that rank simulated events when follow-up resources are limited.
projects.detail: A RAPID-inspired GRU and forest model use matched three-day PLAsTiCC observations. In one independent simulated test, both missed the two targets at the 5% follow-up budget. No performance on observed astronomical events is claimed.
